name: stopful
description: Stopful renders a multi-stop road trip planned in conversation as an interactive, editable map: numbered stops, colour-coded drive legs with times and distances, a day-by-day view, and a link to the full planner. Remote MCP server, one tool (plot_trip), no sign-in.

interface.shortDescription: Road trips on an editable map
interface.longDescription:
Stopful turns a road trip you plan in conversation into a real, interactive map instead of a list of place names.

Give it the stops in driving order and it draws the driving route between them, with the time and distance for every leg, numbered stops and colour-coded days. The map appears directly in the conversation, and a link opens the same trip in the full Stopful planner.

The map is editable. Drag a pin to move a stop, or drag the route itself to add one, and the change is saved to the trip, so when ChatGPT adjusts the trip later, the version you shaped is the one it builds on.

A day-by-day itinerary becomes a day view over the map: pick a day to see that day's driving and activities. Tapping a stop or a leg opens its details, including drive time, a fuel or charging estimate and things to see nearby. Flight and train legs are drawn as such rather than as roads, and the map shows an estimate of what the trip could cost before anything is booked.

There is no AI on the Stopful side: ChatGPT does the planning, and Stopful draws it. No account or sign-in is needed.

Limits: Stopful draws routes with at least two places. It does not book or sell anything; links to hotels and tickets open the provider's own site.
capabilities: Draw a multi-stop driving route on an interactive map
Show drive time and distance for every leg
Show a day-by-day itinerary as a day view over the map
Update the same trip in place as the plan changes
Keep the traveller's own map edits (dragged pins, added stops)
Draw flight and train legs between stops
Estimate the trip's cost before anything is booked
Open the trip in the full Stopful planner via a link
defaultPrompt: Plan a 10-day road trip through Tuscany and put it on a map.
Map a Lisbon to the Pyrenees drive with six stops, two nights each.
Plan a week in the Dolomites with a day-by-day itinerary on a map.

positive.description: Plot a new multi-stop road trip.
positive.prompt: Plan a 10-day road trip through Tuscany with six stops and put it on a map.
positive.expected_behavior: An inline interactive map with six numbered stops in driving order, colour-coded drive legs with time and distance for each, and a link that opens the same trip on stopful.com. The result includes the trip id.

positive.description: Update the trip from the previous case in place. Run directly after case 1, in the same conversation.
positive.expected_behavior: plot_trip is called with the trip id from case 1. The same map and the same link now include Siena in driving order, with the route redrawn. No second trip is created.

positive.prompt: Plan a week in the Dolomites with a day-by-day itinerary and put it on a map.
positive.expected_behavior: The map opens with a day selector. Choosing a day highlights that day's driving, shows its activities as numbered pins, and greys the rest of the route.

positive.description: Show one day of an existing trip on the same map. Run directly after case 3, in the same conversation.
positive.prompt: Show me day 3 on the map.
positive.expected_behavior: plot_trip is called with the trip id from case 3 and focusDay 3. The same trip opens on day 3 with that day's activities and driving highlighted. No new trip is created.

positive.description: A traveller's own map edit survives a later change by ChatGPT. Run after case 1, in the same conversation.
positive.prompt: (First drag one of the stop pins on the inline map to a nearby spot.) Now add Lucca to the trip.
positive.expected_behavior: Lucca is added to the same trip, and the pin that was dragged stays where it was put rather than snapping back.

negative.description: A single destination has no route to draw, so the plugin should not act.
negative.prompt: Find me a hotel in Paris for next weekend.
negative.expected_behavior: plot_trip is not called. ChatGPT answers the hotel question itself; there is no multi-stop route to put on a map.

negative.description: A general travel question with no itinerary.
negative.prompt: What's the weather usually like in Rome in October?
negative.expected_behavior: plot_trip is not called. ChatGPT answers the question directly.

negative.description: Booking and payment are out of scope: the plugin has no booking or payment tool.
negative.prompt: Book the hotels for my Tuscany trip and pay with my saved card.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool books or charges anything. ChatGPT says it cannot make bookings or take payments through Stopful, and that hotels are booked on the provider's own site.

review.commerce_description: Stopful sells nothing and takes no payments in ChatGPT. The map can link out to hotel, ticket and car-hire search results on the providers' own websites (for example Booking.com and Tiqets), opened in the browser through stopful.com; Stopful may earn an affiliate commission on bookings made there, as disclosed in its privacy policy. Nothing is purchased inside the plugin.

publication.release_notes: Resubmission addressing the privacy review. The plot_trip result now returns only the fields declared in its output schema: trip name, start date, party size, each stop's name, coordinates, nights and travel mode, the day titles, and each activity's name, day, time, note, coordinates and pin placement. Fields the Stopful planner saves on a trip (such as hotel details, booking confirmation numbers, notes, ticket prices and links) are no longer passed through when an existing trip is re-read or updated. The privacy policy (https://stopful.com/privacy.html, section 'AI assistants') now lists every category the tool receives, stores and returns, including the private editing key in the map link and children's ages in the party size, and the third-party services the inline map calls. The tool is also now annotated destructiveHint: true, because an update with an id overwrites that trip.
